# The surface

What the code offers, read out of the code: the routes and the grants that guard them, the extensions a boot
installs, and the numbers a caller may spend against. Every table here is rendered, so a route or a grant that is
wrong is a `npm run gen:surface:check` failure in the pull request that made it wrong, rather than a stale list
someone trusts later. Where a behaviour goes, as opposed to what exists, is [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](ARCHITECTURE.md).

## A. HTTP routes, and the grant that guards each

One row per plain-string route literal in `src/server/main.ts` and `src/server/admin.ts` — every
`url.pathname === "…"` and `url.pathname.startsWith("…")`. A path built from a constant is not a literal and so is
not a row: the connector's socket and its attachment endpoints are `CONNECTOR_PATH` in `main.ts`, and they are
listed below, with the other doors that answer without the owner's token.

`exact` is `===`, `prefix` is `startsWith`; a `!==` is not a route and is not a row. The guard is the
`requireGrant`, or the inline `hasGrant` for a route that filters rather than refuses, found in the block the
literal opens, or in a block above it that this path enters — the `/api/` gate is one `if` that closes, and every
route under it is served after the block ended — or, failing that, in the handler it delegates to. When the block
is a dispatcher, the row names the handler it hands the route to and `delegated to` says which; `filtered per area`
means that handler refuses the grant for the areas it owns and hands the device's grants to a function that filters
the payload instead (the panel's `state` and `control` answer a device holding `conversation`, which
`test/panel.test.ts` pins). A literal with no guard stops the generator, which is the point: a route added without
a `requireGrant` is unauthenticated by omission. A path matched in several places is one row, the first, when the
guard is the same — which is sometimes a predicate (`isShellPath`) rather than the handler that serves it. A path
behind two doors keeps two rows: `/api/admin/` passes the server's `authenticate` and then the panel's own grant,
and both are true.

| Route | Match | Guard | Route at | Guarded at |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/api/` | prefix | `authenticate` | `src/server/main.ts:302` | `src/server/main.ts:303` |
| `/api/session` | exact | `authenticate` | `src/server/main.ts:330` | `src/server/main.ts:303` |
| `/api/admin/` | prefix | `authenticate` | `src/server/main.ts:345` | `src/server/main.ts:303` |
| `/api/admin` | exact | `authenticate` | `src/server/main.ts:346` | `src/server/main.ts:303` |
| `/api/permissions` | exact | `authenticate` | `src/server/main.ts:347` | `src/server/main.ts:303` |
| `/api/permissions/` | prefix | `authenticate` | `src/server/main.ts:348` | `src/server/main.ts:303` |
| `/api/status` | exact | `conversation` | `src/server/main.ts:364` | `src/server/main.ts:365` |
| `/api/integrations` | exact | `admin` | `src/server/main.ts:379` | `src/server/main.ts:380` |
| `/api/health` | exact | public — the liveness probe: `ok` and the boot's root id, so an unpaired browser can tell a dead server from a wrong token | `src/server/main.ts:387` | not gated |
| `/` | exact | public — the panel's static shell: a bundle with no secrets in it, and where an unpaired browser is told so | `src/server/main.ts:564` | not gated |
| `/index.html` | exact | public — the same shell, by its file name | `src/server/main.ts:564` | not gated |
| `/admin` | exact | public — the same shell: `/admin` is a door into one page, not a second one | `src/server/main.ts:564` | not gated |
| `/admin/` | exact | public — the same shell, with the trailing slash | `src/server/main.ts:564` | not gated |
| `/api/permissions` | exact | `approve` (delegated to `handlePermissions`) | `src/server/admin.ts:99` | `src/server/admin.ts:555` |
| `/api/permissions/` | prefix | `approve` (delegated to `handlePermissions`) | `src/server/admin.ts:99` | `src/server/admin.ts:555` |
| `/api/admin/` | prefix | `admin`, filtered per area (delegated to `handleAdmin`) | `src/server/admin.ts:103` | `src/server/admin.ts:154` |

## Doors that answer without the owner's token

Each of these is in the generator's `PUBLIC_ROUTES` with its reason, and nothing may be added there without a
sentence a reviewer can argue with. The list is also the whole answer to "which paths answer without a token",
which is why the connector's two paths are here although they are constant-built and never a row.

| Route | Why it is public |
|---|---|
| `/api/health` | the liveness probe: `ok` and the boot's root id, so an unpaired browser can tell a dead server from a wrong token |
| `/api/connector` | the connector's socket, authenticated as the connector by its own credential (`main.ts`, `CONNECTOR_PATH`) |
| `/api/connector/attachments` | the connector's attachment bytes, the same credential on every request (`main.ts`, `CONNECTOR_PATH`) |
| `/` | the panel's static shell: a bundle with no secrets in it, and where an unpaired browser is told so |
| `/index.html` | the same shell, by its file name |
| `/admin` | the same shell: `/admin` is a door into one page, not a second one |
| `/admin/` | the same shell, with the trailing slash |

## B. Extensions a boot installs

`BASE_EXTENSIONS` in `src/server/runtime.ts`, with every name read off the objects rather than out of the source.

| Extension | Tools | Prompt sections | Hook tasks |
|---|---|---|---|
| `coding-tools` | `read`, `write`, `edit`, `bash` | -- | -- |
| `prompt` | -- | `preamble`, `cwd`, `proactive_guidelines`, `team`, `skills`, `profile`, `generative_ui`, `integrations`, `codemode`, `delivery` | -- |
| `memory` | `remember` | -- | -- |
| `delivery` | `reply` | -- | `pi.generation` |
| `sandboxed-ui` | `generateSandboxedUi` | -- | -- |
| `tool-search` | `tool_search` | -- | -- |

Built per boot rather than declared in the array, so they are listed from their own definitions: the MCP tools are
`MCP_TOOL` in `src/server/mcp.ts` and are the only way a service's tools are reached; the code-mode tool is the one
a script writes; `permissions` contributes no tool at all, only the `beforeTool` gate.

| Extension | Tools | Installed when |
|---|---|---|
| `mcp` | `mcp_search`, `mcp_describe`, `mcp_call` | an integration has a tools face |
| `codemode` | `codemode` | always |
| `permissions` | -- | always |

## C. What a caller may spend

Every exported number in `src/server/limits.ts`: the value is the constant's own, and the meaning is the first
sentence of its comment. The three connector budgets share one comment, so they share one meaning and are counted
separately; the budgets are per class on purpose (`docs/SPEC.md` §4.1c), so a flood in one cannot starve another.

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `JSON_BODY_MAX_BYTES` | `32,768` | A small write's body — a name to claim, a session to open. |
| `FIRE_WINDOW_MS` | `60,000` | The window every fire budget is counted in. |
| `CONNECTOR_SUBMISSION_LIMIT` | `60` | A connector's budgets, per class and per connector. |
| `CONNECTOR_FIRE_LIMIT` | `6` | A connector's budgets, per class and per connector. |
| `CONNECTOR_CONTROL_LIMIT` | `6` | A connector's budgets, per class and per connector. |
